Ice cream stocks scoop up 85% gains from 2026 lows; can RIL roil the party?

Abhinav RanjanNew Delhi

Listen to This Article

India's ice cream market is set to heat up as Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL), the FMCG arm of Reliance Industries Ltd, enters the segment with the launch of its new brand, ‘Bombay Creamery’, with prices starting at ₹10.

 

The entry comes at a time when India's ice cream industry is witnessing a structural shift towards organised consumption, premiumisation, wider distribution and de-seasonalisation of consumption. Analysts said that the explosion of quick-commerce platforms has also helped turn ice cream into a four-quarter consumption category.

 

India's per-capita ice cream consumption stands at approximately 1 to 1.6 litres per year, well below global averages of 2.5 to more than 15 litres in Western markets. Analysts said the low consumption base provides a structural tailwind, which is expanding at a CAGR of over 11 per cent. 

 

 Kwality Wall's, Vadilal stocks

At present, there are a few listed ice cream players on Dalal Street, including Kwality Wall's (India) Ltd and Vadilal Industries Ltd. Both stocks have delivered strong gains in 2026 so far. Kwality Wall's shares have rallied 42 per cent, while Vadilal Industries has gained 50 per cent.

 

From their 2026 low of ₹22.24, touched on March 30,

 Kwality Wall's shareshave zoomed 85 per cent. Likewise,Vadilal Industries shareshave bounced back 80 per cent from their January low of ₹3,996. Q1 performance

The performance of the two companies in Q1 was also strong. Data compiled by Business Standard showed that Kwality Wall's delivered 14.9 per cent organic volume growth in Q1, with Ebitda margin expanding to 12.1 per cent. Vadilal Industries reported 34.2 per cent year-on-year revenue growth and 65.5 per cent growth in operating profit.

Can incumbents retain market share? According to Saurav Chaube, equity research analyst at SAMCO Securities, competition will indeed increase for Kwality Wall's and Vadilal with RCPL's entry. However, established players could sustain their market share as ice cream is different from many other FMCG categories, given the importance of cold-chain infrastructure in distribution.

 

“Established players already have networks and strong regional brands. Reliance, however, has the advantage of a large retail ecosystem, strong distribution capabilities and the ability to invest aggressively,” he said, adding that the immediate impact is likely to be greater on pricing power rather than volumes.

 

Kwality Wall's has the advantage of Unilever's established brands such as Magnum and Cornetto, along with a strong cold-chain network. Vadilal, meanwhile, has a strong value proposition and around 16 per cent share of the organised market, with FY25 revenue of around ₹10.1 billion.

“Reliance's entry at the ₹10 price point is set to intensify price competition. The bigger risk is near-term margin pressure if the industry responds aggressively on pricing,” said Sandeep Abhange, research analyst, consumer & midcaps at LKP Securities.

Unorganised segment Analysts said that Reliance's entry could also intensify competition in the unorganised segment. They argue that the unorganised segment has remained a difficult space even for the established players to penetrate, mainly due to affordability and distribution. But Reliance's pricing power gives it an advantage. Also, Reliance possesses unmatched financial muscle. 

 

“A large portion of the unorganised ice cream sector relies on cheap raw materials with questionable hygiene standards. By offering real-dairy cream products starting at ₹10, Reliance removes the compromise between food safety and affordability, enticing value-conscious buyers to migrate from local mom-and-pop vendors to a trusted brand,” said market expert Avinash Gorakshakar. “Reliance’s biggest competitive advantage is arguably not the ice cream itself but its ecosystem. Its retail footprint, JioMart and distribution capabilities can allow Bombay Creamery to achieve rapid availability at a price point that can attract first-time consumers,” Agrim Verma, smallcase manager, Divitiae Investments said.
